excerpt: Unabyss pulls your context from Slack, Gmail, Notion, GitHub and more into one memory that Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT read over MCP. From $13/month.
content:
Unabyss is a context layer for AI tools. You connect the apps where your work lives, such as Slack, Gmail, Notion, GitHub, Google Drive, Linear and meeting recorders like Fathom, Fireflies and Granola, and Unabyss pulls the information into one structured memory, tagged by topic, sensitivity and source. AI tools that support MCP, including Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex and Gemini, then read the relevant part of that memory, so you do not have to re-explain your role, projects and preferences every time you open a new chat or switch tools. Claude can be connected through an official connector, and the context can also be exported as files.

The site contrasts this with the built-in memory of ChatGPT or Claude, which stays inside one tool, and with a hand-written context file such as CLAUDE.md, which goes stale. Unabyss stays connected to your sources and updates itself. Setup is said to take under 90 seconds. Data is encrypted at rest and in transit, each connection uses OAuth scoped per app, EU users' data is hosted in the EU, and the company says it does not sell your data or use it to train AI models.

Unabyss is run by OneType Prosta Spółka Akcyjna, a company registered in Warsaw, Poland. Paid plans start at $13 a month billed annually, each with a 7-day free trial and no card needed. It has launched on Product Hunt more than once, including as Unabyss for Claude.

Unabyss launched on Product Hunt on 17 July 2026 and finished #1 for the day, with 588 upvotes and 132 comments (as of 14 October 2026). An earlier launch of Unabyss on 25 May 2026 also finished #1 for the day, with 705 upvotes and 145 comments.

We have not tested Unabyss ourselves. This page brings together its official site, privacy policy and terms, its Product Hunt listing and the official pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Web app with MCP server for AI tools
profile.starts_at: 7-day free trial, then Pro from $13/month billed annually
profile.summary_short: One self-updating memory from your work apps, shared with Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor over MCP
use_cases: Giving Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT the same picture of your role and projects without re-pasting it
Replacing hand-maintained context files such as CLAUDE.md that go out of date
Pulling meeting notes from Fathom, Fireflies, tl;dv or Granola into the context your AI sees
Sharing one company context across a team's AI tools on the Team plan
Choosing which AI tool may see which slice of your context

fit: use several AI tools (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT and others) and are tired of repeating yourself
keep your work in Slack, Gmail, Notion, GitHub or Google Drive and want AI to read it
are on a team that wants a shared, up-to-date context for its AI agents
not_fit: use only one AI tool and its built-in memory is enough for you
cannot let a third-party service read your email, chat or documents
want a free plan: every plan is paid after the 7-day trial

pricing.intro: Prices are from Unabyss's own site, in US dollars. Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial with no credit card required, and annual billing saves up to 20%.

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: For individuals: up to 3 connected agents via MCP, up to 20 connected accounts, premium usage tier

plans.name: Max
plans.detail: Unlimited agents, connected accounts and usage, multi-account support for Google apps, early access to new features. The site suggests it for people on Claude's Max plan

plans.name: Team
plans.price: $39 per seat a month billed annually ($49 shown alongside)
plans.detail: Everything in Max for each seat, a shared team workspace, central seat and invoice management; minimum 3 seats

notes: The pricing card shows two figures for each plan (for example $13 and $15) next to the words 'billed annually'; we read the lower figure as the annual rate. Check the pricing toggle on the site before buying.

alternatives.intro: Built-in memory in ChatGPT and Claude is the obvious free option, but it stays inside one tool. These are other memory layers for AI. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Supermemory
items.what: Memory and search API that gives AI agents persistent, searchable memory
items.starts_at: Free with $5 of monthly credits; Pro $19/month
items.difference: Aimed at developers building agents through an API, rather than a ready-made context layer you connect your apps to.

items.name: Mem0
items.what: Memory layer for AI agents and LLM apps
items.difference: A developer platform for adding memory to your own AI apps; Unabyss is built for people who want their existing AI tools to share context.

alternatives.more: ChatGPT Memory, Claude's memory and hand-written context files are the do-it-yourself options Unabyss compares itself with on its site.

pros: Works across many AI tools through MCP rather than locking memory into one
Connects 25+ apps, including email, chat, docs, code and meeting recorders
Context is tagged by sensitivity and you choose what each AI tool can see
EU hosting for EU users; the company says data is not used to train AI models
cons: No free plan after the trial
You give a third party OAuth access to your email, chat and documents
SOC 2 Type II is listed as in progress, not complete
The pricing card's two figures per plan are easy to misread

posts.author: Marcin Uchacz
posts.text: Launch post explaining that the team built Unabyss after tiring of keeping many .md context files up to date across Claude, Cursor and OpenClaw.

faq.a: A context layer for AI. It pulls information from apps such as Slack, Gmail, Notion and GitHub into one structured memory that Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT and other MCP-compatible tools can read.
Pro starts at $13 a month billed annually, Max at $79 and Team at $39 per seat (minimum three seats). Every plan has a 7-day free trial with no card required.

faq.q: How is it different from ChatGPT or Claude memory?
faq.a: Built-in memory stays inside one tool. Unabyss takes context from where your work lives and serves it to any MCP-compatible tool, so it follows you between Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT.
Yes. The site offers an official Claude connector, and you can also connect Cursor, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP or export context files.

Unabyss says context is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3), each connection uses scoped OAuth that you can revoke, EU users get EU-hosted data, and data is not sold or used to train AI models.
Built-in memory in ChatGPT or Claude, hand-written context files, or developer memory platforms such as Supermemory and Mem0.
